atomic_requirement: Sets rules protecting natural persons regarding personal-data processing and the free movement of such data.
Applies to personal data processed wholly/partly by automated means and manual processing.
Applies to processing by a controller/processor established in the Union, regardless of where processing occurs.
Personal data, processing, controller, processor, recipient, consent, personal data breach, biometrics
CHAPTER II — Principles (Articles 5–11)

article_title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
atomic_requirement:
Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly, transparently, for specified explicit purposes, limited to necessary data,
accurate, kept identifiable no longer than necessary, with appropriate security.

Processing is lawful only if based on consent, contract necessity, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, or legitimate
interests.
Controller must demonstrate consent was given
Consent requests must be in plain language

Data subject can withdraw
consent at any time.
Processing based on child's consent is lawful from age 16
below that, parental authorization is required.

article_title: Processing of special categories of personal data
atomic_requirement:
Prohibits processing revealing racial origin, political opinions, genetic/biometric data, health data unless explicit consent or
legal exception applies.

article_title: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions
atomic_requirement: Permitted only under official authority control or Union/Member State law.

article_title: Processing which does not require identification
atomic_requirement: Controller is not obliged to retain identifying information solely to comply with GDPR

article_title: Processing which does not require identification
atomic_requirement: CHAPTER III — Rights of the Data Subject (Articles 12–23)
Information must be provided concisely, transparently, intelligibly, and in plain language.

article_title: Information to be provided where data is collected from subject
atomic_requirement: Disclose controller identity, DPO contact, processing purposes, legal basis, recipients, retention period, and subject rights.

article_title: Information to be provided where data was not obtained from subject
atomic_requirement: Same disclosures as Art

article_title: Information to be provided where data was not obtained from subject
atomic_requirement: 13 plus categories of data and source.

article_title: Right of access by the data subject
atomic_requirement: Right to obtain confirmation of processing, access to personal data, and details on processing logic.
Inaccurate personal data must be corrected without undue delay.

article_title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
atomic_requirement: Controller must erase personal data without undue delay when data is no longer necessary or consent is withdrawn.
Right to restrict processing where accuracy is contested or processing is unlawful.

article_title: Notification obligation regarding rectification or erasure
atomic_requirement: Controller must notify recipients of data rectification or erasure.
Right to receive personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and transmit to another controller.
Right to object at any time to processing based on legitimate interests or direct marketing.
Right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing/profiling.
Member State law may restrict rights to safeguard national security, defence, public security
CHAPTER IV — Controller and Processor (Articles 24–43)
Implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to demonstrate compliance.

article_title: Data protection by design and by default
atomic_requirement: Build data protection principles into processing design from the outset.
Joint controllers must transparently determine respective responsibilities.

article_title: Representatives of controllers not established in the Union
atomic_requirement: Designate an EU representative where Art

Processing by a processor must be governed by a binding contract specifying subject matter, duration, nature, and
obligations.

article_title: Processing under authority of controller or processor
atomic_requirement: Only process under instructions of controller.
Maintain detailed records of processing activities for organizations over 250 employees or high risk.
Cooperate with supervisory authorities on request.
Implement technical measures including encryption, confidentiality, resilience, and regular vulnerability testing.

article_title: Notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority
atomic_requirement: Notify supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach.

article_title: Communication of personal data breach to data subject
atomic_requirement: Notify data subject without undue delay if breach risks high risk to rights.
Conduct DPIA prior to processing likely to result in high risk.
Consult supervisory authority prior to processing if DPIA indicates high unmitigated risk.
Mandatory DPO for public authorities or large scale monitoring/special category data.
DPO must be properly involved in data protection matters and report to highest management.
Inform, advise, monitor compliance, and act as contact point for supervisory authority.
Encourage codes of conduct to contribute to proper GDPR application.

article_title: Monitoring of approved codes of conduct
atomic_requirement: Monitoring delegated to accredited independent bodies.
Establish certification mechanisms, seals, and marks.
Certification bodies must be accredited
CHAPTER V — Transfers to Third Countries (Articles 44–50)

chapter_title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations
atomic_requirement: Any transfer must satisfy conditions of Chapter V.

chapter_title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations
article_title: Transfers on basis of adequacy decision
atomic_requirement: Allowed where EU Commission decides third country ensures adequate protection.

chapter_title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations
atomic_requirement: Allowed with Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs).

chapter_title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations
atomic_requirement: Approved rules for intra-group international data transfers.

chapter_title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations
article_title: Transfers not authorized by Union law
atomic_requirement: Foreign court orders only enforceable if based on international agreements.

chapter_title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations
atomic_requirement: Derogations for explicit consent, contract performance, or public interest.
